prompts.defenses: Use case: sketch-to-render. Asset type: production multi-view PAINT-OVER texture atlas for a 3D MOBA. The attached image is the EDIT TARGET, not just inspiration. Paint directly onto every gray silhouette in-place, preserving the exact image dimensions, grid, object silhouette, scale, position, orthographic views, gaps and negative space. No perspective change. Four equal columns are FRONT (+Z), BACK (-Z), SIDE (+X), TOP (+Y). All cells depict the same objects from different directions. Keep all empty dark background exactly unchanged. This will be projected back onto the original 3D surfaces, so moving anything breaks the asset. Turn the gray blockout surfaces into polished hand-painted science-fiction architecture for an overgrown NIKKE-style military outpost: sculpted-looking bevel highlights, bold panel divisions, recessed machinery, deep painted crevice occlusion, worn edge glints, subtle brushed-metal strokes, rich cool blue-gray steel, warm ivory ceramic armor and restrained copper/ochre detail. The art must have deliberate stylized painted shading and material depth, like an excellent handcrafted MOBA asset. No photoreal noise, generic gray concrete slab appearance, excessive dirt, text, labels, logos, captions, wireframes or UI. No added objects outside existing silhouettes. Consistent details across all views. Paint details at readable medium scale, not microscopic noise. Do not keep the flat gray lighting from the source. Do not render a new scene or make a concept-art perspective sheet. Output the edited atlas at the same aspect ratio. This atlas has THREE equal rows: row 1 an octagonal armored gun-tower pedestal with a rotating mount at its crown; row 2 a low fortified bunker with two heavy flanking buttresses and a central gun mount; row 3 an upgraded keep bunker with four raised square corner pylons. Preserve the source geometry but richly paint the armor faces: inset maintenance hatches, layered edge trim, protective ribs, mechanical vents, ivory corner armor, steel-blue recessed bays, restrained amber safety marks. TOP cells need fully painted roofs, maintenance grilles, bolted rims and dark machinery sockets aligned to the exact source shapes. This is neutral architecture shared by both teams, so avoid bright red or bright cyan team markings.
